title: AWS Code Tools: CodeCommit, CodeBuild, CodeDeploy, and CodePipeline
description: Build complete CI/CD pipelines using AWS CodeCommit, CodeBuild, CodeDeploy, and CodePipeline.

data.text: AWS Developer Tools is a suite of services that help you build, test, and deploy applications. CodeCommit stores your code, CodeBuild compiles and tests it, CodeDeploy deploys it, and CodePipeline orchestrates the entire flow.

AWS CodeCommit is a fully managed source control service that hosts private Git repositories. It integrates with other AWS services and your existing Git tools. CodeCommit supports pull requests, branching, and triggers.

AWS CodeBuild is a fully managed build service. It compiles your source code, runs tests, and produces artifacts. You define your build process in a buildspec.yml file placed in the root of your source repository.

AWS CodeDeploy automates code deployments to EC2, Lambda, and ECS. It supports multiple deployment strategies, including in-place updates and blue/green deployments. For EC2, you use an appspec.yml file to define deployment actions.

data.title: CodeDeploy Deployment Strategies
items: **In-place** — updates the existing instance, potentially causing downtime
**Blue/Green** — deploys to a new environment and switches traffic, zero downtime
**Linear** — shifts traffic in equal increments over time

data.text: AWS CodePipeline is a continuous delivery service that orchestrates your build, test, and deploy stages. Each stage contains one or more actions, such as pulling source code, building with CodeBuild, or deploying with CodeDeploy.

data.title: Example buildspec.yml for CodeBuild
data.content: This buildspec.yml defines a build phase that runs tests and a post-build phase that uploads an artifact.
data.code:
version: 0.2

phases:
  install:
    runtime-versions:
      python: 3.11
    commands:
      - pip install -r requirements.txt
  build:
    commands:
      - echo "Running tests..."
      - pytest tests/
      - echo "Building application..."
      - python -m build
  post_build:
    commands:
      - echo "Build completed on `date`"

artifacts:
  files:
    - '**/*'
  base-directory: dist

terms.definition: Continuous Integration and Continuous Deployment — automating the process from code commit to production deployment.
A YAML file that tells CodeBuild how to build, test, and package your application.
A YAML file used by CodeDeploy to define what to install and which lifecycle events to run during deployment.
A deployment strategy where a new version is deployed alongside the old version, and traffic is switched over.

data.title: Build a CI/CD Pipeline
data.description: Create a CodePipeline that pulls code from CodeCommit, builds it with CodeBuild, and deploys it with CodeDeploy to an EC2 instance.
steps: Create a CodeCommit repository and push sample code
Create an EC2 instance with the CodeDeploy agent installed
Create a CodeDeploy application and deployment group
Create a CodePipeline connecting all three stages
data.expectedOutcome: Your pipeline automatically builds and deploys your application every time you push code.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: CodeCommit stores your code in private Git repositories
CodeBuild compiles, tests, and packages your application
CodeDeploy automates deployments with multiple strategies
CodePipeline orchestrates the entire CI/CD workflow
data.takeaway: AWS Code Tools provide a complete CI/CD pipeline without third-party tools, all integrated with IAM and CloudWatch.
